spec: CONTROL.md §14.7 (a held session, the machine's caps)
note: A rule that continues a session a window holds waits until nothing holds it, within the notice's expiry; it never forks a copy and never hands the words to the window. A start counts against the machine's caps on starts (2 running, 10 an hour by default), which a receiver's starts and asks share, and waits for them the same way. A waiting notice is acked `taken` once, and its final ack follows. A run counts against its rule's cap and cooldown when it is taken, the count is given back when it ends without running, and the folder, the harness and the session are checked again when it is let go. A `machine` step is the person changing the machine's settings at its terminal. A deadline is exclusive: at its own instant a waiting run has expired, before anything else that happens at that instant. The machine's caps count starts as a local ask's do: at most 2 in progress and 10 in a sliding hour; a continued session takes no start but a headless slot (3), and waits for one the same way, refused `start_limit` at its deadline. A rule runs one at a time: its next run waits behind its last, refused `busy` at its deadline, and waiting runs of one rule go in the order they were taken.
